Title: Document 4
Content: Source: Declaration of the Assembly of the Clergy of France,* `text(1682)`

Saint Peter and his successors, the vicars of Jesus Christ [the popes], and the entire church have received their power from God only in spiritual matters that concern salvation, but not in temporal and civil matters. . . . We declare as a result that kings and sovereigns are not subjected by the order of God to any ecclesiastical authority in temporal matters; that kings cannot be deposed either directly or indirectly by authority of the head of the church; that kings’ subjects cannot be released from their duty of submission and obedience or absolved from their oath of fidelity; and that this doctrine, necessary for the public peace and equally advantageous for the church and for the state, must be inviolably followed because it is in conformity with the Word of God, with the tradition of the Holy Fathers, and with the examples of the saints.
References: An assembly called by Louis `text(XIV)` in response to a dispute between the king and the pope concerning the king’s appointment of bishops
